newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end up amid speculative, fund buying.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end up amid speculative, fund buying.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled higher for the second straight session, buoyed by speculative and fund buying that lifted July to a seven-week high, trading sources said.
The benchmark contract closed up 1.40 cents at 81.90 cents a lb, traded 80.50 to 84.35 cents, its highest level since reaching 84.60 cents March 27. The rest finished 1.00 and 1.20 cents higher.
Analysts said gains were driven by technical factors, adding that the supply and demand picture remains unchanged.

With Brazil and the U.S. expected to produce record crops in the 1997/98 season, and high retail prices continuing to dampen demand for juice in the U.S., the market is not likely to climb much higher, they said.
"Processors and storage facilities say they have no room to hold more juice, so supply is not a problem," a Florida-based broker said.
Florida Citrus Processors' Association will issue its weekly movement number after the close.
Tecnically, resistance was pegged at a gap between 84.90 and 85.00 cents, followed by 88.00 cents, for July juice. Support was seen at 74.00 cents.
Volume was estimated at 5,000 lots against Wednesday's official 1,742 lots.
